title: Ego to fixed third-person tabletop replay, SIM v35 and DiT v8

observations: The clock, small blue cylinder, and tall cylinder remain identifiable through the full sequence.
The fixed third-person camera, background, torso, arms, and action order remain visually continuous.
SIM and DiT event neighborhoods were compared for the clock release, blue-cylinder carry and release, and tall-cylinder grip/carry/final hold.

timing.method: Monotone C1 PCHIP output-to-source map with nearest original-frame selection; no optical-flow synthesis and no new H3 or SIM generation.

implemented: Consumed-output numerical gates and bounded temporary-memory statistics
In-process multi-request resident H3 worker with independent cache epochs
Cooperative same-NUMA four-GPU UUID selection and leases
not_claimed: Matched real-H3 warm-request speedup for the new resident/same-NUMA path

limitations: One historical real tabletop scene; no additional-scene end-to-end acceptance
Not unattended raw-RGB calibration or a built-in autonomous VLM
Visual overlap and imposed contact constraints are not exact 3-D contact, force closure, or collision certification
Nearest-frame retiming can introduce visible cadence changes
The unchanged EGO/SIM labels describe source content and timing; the three-panel delivery is a lossy H.264 encode, not pixel-identical preservation
